newsitem.title: USA: US spot natgas down about 50 cts from Aug indices.
newsitem.headline: US spot natgas down about 50 cts from Aug indices.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices for September dove about 50 cents under August indices Tuesday, pressured by expectations for cooler weather late next month and light bidweek buying interest, industry sources said.
Louisiana Gulf Coast prices for September 1 delivery softened into the $1.75-1.80 per million British thermal units area, with Henry Hub quoted mostly in the low-$1.80s.
Several traders speculated that some buyers may be waiting until after the upcoming Labor Day Holiday before making the bulk of their purchases, thereby keeping the lid on prices.
In the Midcontinent, September pricing hovered in the $1.60s, down from the $2.10-2.15 range for August 1.
The softening Gulf market also filtered into the West Texas markets, where traders reported closing most Permian basin deals for next month in the high-$1.50s to low-$1.60s.
August Permian prices carried about a five-cent premium in the low-to-mid $1.60s.
In the Appalachian region, September prices were talked in the low-to-mid $1.90s, down about 50 cents from August indices.
-- H McCulloch, New York Power Desk +212-859-1628
